body: **Summary:** FMCG companies sell branded, frequently purchased goods through a distribution network that reaches ~8–10 million outlets. Profit comes from brand-led pricing power, gross margin over commodities (palm oil, crude derivatives, milk, wheat, cocoa) and scale in advertising and distribution. Negative working capital and asset-light models drive RoCE of 50–100%+. Key metrics: underlying volume growth (UVG), price/mix growth, gross margin, EBITDA margin, A&P % of sales, rural against urban growth, distribution reach (direct outlets), market share (NielsenIQ), and channel mix (modern trade, e-commerce, quick commerce). Cycle drivers: rural income (monsoon, MSP, rural wages), food inflation (which squeezes discretionary spend), commodity cycles, GST changes (Sep 2025 rate rationalisation), competition from D2C and regional brands, and quick commerce. Lead indicators: NielsenIQ quarterly FMCG volume tracker, rural wage data (Labour Bureau), MGNREGA demand, IMD monsoon, CPI food, tractor and 2W sales as rural proxies. Winners (HUL, Nestle, Britannia over 2000–2020) kept volume-led growth, category creation, premiumisation and distribution depth. Losers were companies that relied on price-led growth, failed to adapt to new channels or made diversification bets. Valuation: P/E 40–60x for leaders. The peak came in 2019–21, and multiples have since compressed as growth slowed. FMCG P/E was 33.8 in Jun 2026 against a 7-year median of 41.8. Nov 2026: Q2 FY27 FMCG value growth was a six-quarter high of 8.6%, with rural at 10.6% against urban at 5.8%, and HUL UVG ~7%. Traps: paying 60x for 4% volume growth, and pricing-led quarters. Sources: [1](https://www.sahi.com/news/india-fmcg-value-growth-hits-six-quarter-high-of-8-6-in-q2fy27-on-rural-surge) · [2](https://ticker.finology.in/discover/market-update/hul-q2-fy27-results-analysis) · [3](https://www.indexpe.in/blog/nifty-sector-valuations-june-2026) Links: about `insight:myth-titan-3`
